summary: Implemented 14 of the 16 endpoints in this task's contract for the life-cycle-uc8-uc9 module: Document tab (GET document, GET document/download), Versions tab, the immutable Activity Log, Folder/Tag assignment (POST contracts/{id}/folder-tags, GET /folder-tags), the full Obligations & Renewal screen (list/create/update/accept obligations, GET renewal panel), and the Renew/Amend/Terminate lifecycle actions -- all against the real `contracts`/`contract_lifecycle.py` persistence the T-00-FOUNDATION-API task already built, via new app/schemas/repositories/services/routers/contract_lifecycle.py files that do not touch any file belonging to another module. Enforced role + ownership/assignment access control per UC8-BR-001/007/008/009/010, the Executed/Active gate on Obligations & Renewal (UC9-AF-002), obligation status-transition rules and evidence requirement (UC9-BR-013/014), lazy Overdue auto-transition (UC9-BR-002/015), AI Suggested -> Confirmed labelling (UC9-BR-005), the 90/60/30-day renewal alert banner (UC9-BR-003), single-in-flight-action locking (UC9-BR-008), and the Renew/Amend/Terminate linked-contract creation with cross-references and audit trail (UC9-BR-006/007/016/017/018). CLAUDE.md wins on HOW per the task's own precedence rule, so verification used `python -m compileall app tests alembic` and `pytest -q` (not `dotnet build`/`dotnet test`, which do not apply to this Python/FastAPI/PostgreSQL repo) -- both pass, 303/303 tests green (up from 280 before this task), including a new tests/test_contract_lifecycle.py exercising every implemented endpoint's happy path, 400, 401, 403, 404 and 409 cases plus the obligation/renewal business rules above. The two endpoints that are NOT implemented -- GET /api/v1/contracts and GET /api/v1/contracts/{contractId} -- collide at the exact (method, path) level with endpoints uc123's T-CONTRACTS-API run already shipped (app/routers/contracts.py, app/services/contracts.py) under different roles and DTO shapes; see blockers for why these were left to uc123's existing implementation rather than silently overridden or duplicated into unreachable dead routes.

pr.title: feat(life-cycle-uc8-uc9): Document/Versions/Activity-Log/Folder-Tag/Obligations/Renewal endpoints
pr.body: Implements 14 of 16 T-CONTRACTS-API endpoints for the life-cycle-uc8-uc9 module (UC8/UC9 stories): Document tab, Versions tab, immutable Activity Log, Folder/Tag assignment, the full Obligations & Renewal screen, and Renew/Amend/Terminate. GET /api/v1/contracts and GET /api/v1/contracts/{contractId} are not implemented -- they collide at the exact (method, path) level with endpoints uc123's earlier T-CONTRACTS-API run already shipped under different roles/DTOs; see this task's blockers for the full detail. `python -m compileall` and `pytest -q` both pass (303/303).

blockers: Hard path collision, not implemented: this task's context.json calls for 'GET /api/v1/contracts' (ContractSearchRequest -> paged ContractListItemResponse, roles TENANT_ADMIN/CONTRACT_OWNER/LEGAL_REVIEWER/APPROVER) and 'GET /api/v1/contracts/{contractId}' (-> ContractDetailResponse, same roles). Both paths, at the exact same (method, path), are already implemented and live for the uc123 module (app/routers/contracts.py's `list_contracts`/`get_contract`, backed by app/services/contracts.py, docstring-attributed to an earlier run of this same task id T-CONTRACTS-API) with a different DTO shape (ContractListItemResponse there has id/contractType/contractOwnerName/... vs this contract's contractId/counterparty/owner/folderTags/indexingInProgress) and a different role list (uc123's also allows SIGNER). FastAPI/Starlette routes are matched by (method, path) across the whole app in router-inclusion order -- a second router registering the identical path is permanently unreachable, so there is no way to 'add the new path beside it' as CLAUDE.md's module-addition section prescribes; the only alternatives were (a) silently rewrite/replace uc123's existing GET handlers (forbidden: 'never rewrite... code belonging to a module you were not asked to touch'), or (b) register a second, permanently-dead implementation that would mislead both tests and the OpenAPI doc. I chose neither: I left uc123's existing GET /contracts and GET /contracts/{contractId} untouched and did not implement this module's versions of those two paths. All 14 other endpoints in this task's contract (document, document/download, versions, activity-log, folder-tags POST, /folder-tags GET, obligations GET/POST/PATCH/accept, renewal GET, renew/amend/terminate) are fully implemented against the real tables and covered by tests.

Missing/underspecified field: 'the system's supported upload size from UC2' (UC8-BR-006, Disable Download for Oversized Documents) is referenced by every oversized-document acceptance criterion but never given a literal number anywhere in this task's context.json, TASK.md, or the tables it reads. Used 25 MiB (26,214,400 bytes) as app/services/contract_lifecycle.py's OVERSIZED_FILE_BYTES constant -- a judgement call, not sourced from any UC2 contract I was given access to.

Contract/table type mismatch, resolved by interpretation: context.json types `CreateObligationRequest.owner` and `UpdateObligationRequest.owner` as `string`, but the `obligations` table's corresponding column is `owner_id` (UUID FK to `users`, per context.json's own table definition) and the stories describe the Owner field as a dropdown of existing tenant users (UC9-FV-001/MF-001), not free text. Interpreted the `owner` string field as carrying the selected user's UUID in string form (parsed via `uuid.UUID(owner)`, 400 on parse failure) rather than as a display name, since there is no column to persist an arbitrary free-text owner distinct from a user reference. `ObligationResponse.owner` (also typed `string` in the contract) is populated by resolving that id back to the user's name for display.

Missing table/column, minimal representation chosen: UC9-BR-003's Renewal Alert Banner must fire separately for the Contract End Date and for the 'Notice Period deadline', but `contracts.notice_period` (persisted as `notice_period_text`, see T-00-FOUNDATION-API's blockers) is a free-text VARCHAR(100) (e.g. '30 days'), not a structured duration -- there is no column anywhere in this task's tables that stores a numeric notice-period length. Implemented `_parse_notice_period_days` to regex out the first integer in that text and compute the deadline as `end_date - that many days`; text with no leading integer (e.g. 'See Section 4') silently skips only the Notice Period alert (the Contract End Date alert still fires independently, per the stories' 'independent of any End Date alert' requirement).

Business-rule judgement call: no scheduler/cron exists anywhere in this repo to implement UC9-BR-002/BR-015's 'automatically changes Status to Overdue' as a background process. Applied the Overdue transition lazily and persists it (not just display-only) the next time any obligation on the contract is read via GET /obligations, GET /renewal, PATCH .../obligations/{id}, or POST .../obligations/{id}/accept -- functionally equivalent for a request/response API with no out-of-band automation, but not a true 'the instant the due date passes' transition.

Business-rule judgement call: the Renew/Amend/Terminate actions in this service execute synchronously and complete within one request (create the linked contract + flip the original's status, all in one commit) rather than being a long-running async workflow. `contracts.renewal_action_in_progress` is still set and checked (UC9-BR-008's single-in-flight-action lock is enforced: a second attempt on a contract whose status is no longer Executed/Active after the first action is rejected with 409), but because there is no real concurrency window within a single synchronous request, two literally-simultaneous requests racing the same contract row are not deadlock-safe beyond whatever isolation the underlying database session provides -- there is no explicit row lock (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) taken.

Added field, not in context.json: `LinkedContractActionResponse.linkedContractReference` and `linkedContractId` are both typed `uuid` in the contract with no table column distinguishing them -- `contract_lifecycle_actions` only stores one `linked_contract_id`. Populated both response fields with the same value (the newly created linked contract's id) since no second, distinct reference value exists anywhere in the persisted schema.

Shared-column extension: additively extended `app/schemas/contract.py`'s `ContractStatus` Literal (uc123's shared response-validation enum for the `contracts.status` column) with `In Approval`, `In Signature`, `Active`, `Expired`, `Terminated`, `Renewed`, `Amended` -- this module's stories require all of these as valid lifecycle states (UC8-BR-011, UC9-BR-004/016/017/018) and without this change, uc123's own `GET /api/v1/contracts/{id}` would 500 on any contract this module transitions into one of those states. Followed the precedent already established in that file's comments by the approvals and e-signature modules' prior runs, which did the same for their own new statuses.

Could not verify any of this task's endpoints end-to-end against a live PostgreSQL instance: this sandbox has no reachable Postgres and starting one via `docker run postgres:16-alpine` requires interactive approval that did not resolve during this autonomous run (same limitation T-00-FOUNDATION-API's blockers already documented for this environment). Mitigated the same way: booted the app live with uvicorn on port 5199 (DATABASE_URL unset, so migrations-at-startup is a documented no-op) and confirmed /health (200), 401 (missing X-User-Role), and 403 (disallowed role) all work without a database, and confirmed via /openapi.json that all 14 implemented routes are registered with the correct methods and that GET /api/v1/contracts and GET /api/v1/contracts/{id} resolve only to uc123's existing handlers. Full behavioral coverage (every endpoint's happy path, 400, 403, 404, 409) was instead exercised against a real relational database via tests/test_contract_lifecycle.py's in-memory SQLite fixtures (the same approach every other test file in this repo already uses) -- 303/303 tests pass. A live Postgres run is still recommended before this is trusted in production.
